title: LethAL doctor --json output
description: What `lethal doctor --config <path> --json` prints on stdout. Versioned by doctorSchemaVersion: bumped when a field is renamed, removed or changes meaning, or when a value domain changes in either direction. Additive fields do not bump it, so a consumer must tolerate properties it does not know. Exit code 0 means no check failed, 1 means at least one failed; the code is the gate, not this document. A check can be skipped (`checks[].skipped`, R253) without failing; before R253 none could be, so every older report reads the same under either wording.

doctorSchemaVersion.description: The version of THIS document's structure.

ok.description: True when no check failed. Mirrors the exit code. A skipped check (`checks[].skipped`) does not fail, and was not verified: read it before trusting a true.

checks.description: One entry per check actually run. A check omitted for the config shape is absent rather than passing; the caveat says which and why.

detail.description: What was observed, never just "ok". Prose for a human; do not parse it.

skipped.description: R253: present when doctor could not ask at all, for a reason the config names (`detail` says which, and the fix, e.g. no `bcdev.apiBaseUrl` on BC on Linux). `ok` is then `true`: nothing failed and nothing was verified.

notChecked.description: What doctor does NOT check, on every invocation. This is the part that matters when `ok` is true: a green report does not cover these.

caveat.description: Present only when the config shape triggers one. Says which checks were skipped and why.

note.description: The same sentence the console prints. Prose, and not contractual.
